text:
Shipbuilders Look to Hydrogen

The world's largest shipbuilders are racing to develop vessels powered by hydrogen, which emits no carbon dioxide when burned. Progress has, [1], been slower than the industry predicted, largely because hydrogen must be stored at very low temperatures and occupies far more space than conventional fuel.

[2] Engineers at Sorensen Marine believe they have found a partial solution. Their design places the fuel tanks in the hull rather than on deck, thereby [3] cargo capacity by only five percent. The company's chief engineer concedes that the technology will not be commercially viable [4] a global network of refueling ports exists.

questions.explanation: The sentence contrasts the race to develop hydrogen vessels with slow progress; 'however' marks the contrast.

choices: The storage problem has proved the least stubborn obstacle, and it has absorbed a disproportionate share of research budgets.
The storage problem has proved the most stubborn obstacle, and it has absorbed a disproportionate share of research budgets.
The storage problem has proved the most stubborn obstacle, and it has been solved by a disproportionate share of vessels.
The fuel problem will prove the most stubborn obstacle, and it absorbed a disproportionate share of research budgets.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says engineers 'believe they have found a partial solution', so the previous one should present a problem; the first does. The others call it the least stubborn, say it was solved, or mismatch tenses.
'Thereby reducing cargo capacity' is a participle phrase giving the result of the design; the other forms are not possible after 'thereby'.
The technology will not be viable 'until' a network exists; 'unless' would need a different structure, and the others do not fit.

text:
Whitby Regional Hospital – Information for Visitors

Visiting is permitted between 2 p.m. and 8 p.m. on general wards, [1] visiting hours in the intensive care unit are set by the nurse in charge. Visitors are asked to limit themselves to two per patient at any one time.

[2] Children under twelve may visit only with the agreement of the ward sister, and anyone who has experienced symptoms of infection within the previous forty-eight hours should [3] from visiting. Flowers are not permitted on any ward, [4] they pose a risk of infection to patients with weakened immune systems.

questions.explanation: 'Whereas visiting hours in the intensive care unit are set by the nurse' contrasts the general rule with the unit's rule.

choices: These restrictions are intended to protect visitors who are especially resistant to infection and to allow staff to work without supervision.
These restrictions are intended to protect patients who are especially vulnerable to infection and to allow staff to work without obstruction.
These restrictions are intended to protect staff who are especially vulnerable to injury and to allow patients to work without obstruction.
These permissions are intended to protect patients who are especially vulnerable to infection and to allow families to visit without limit.
questions.explanation: The following sentences set conditions for children, symptoms and flowers, which are restrictions; the first option introduces them. The others reverse the aim or use 'permissions'.
'Refrain from visiting' is the fixed expression meaning not visit; 'retreat', 'retain' and 'refuse' do not take 'from visiting' this way.
'As they pose a risk of infection' gives the reason for the ban on flowers; the others do not give reasons.

text:
To: Participants in the Graduate Programme
From: Seraphina Quill, Talent Development
Subject: Rotation placements

I am pleased to confirm your second placement, which begins on 1 June. Each of you will spend six months in a department that differs from your first, [1] that you gain a broad understanding of the business before specializing.

[2] The allocation was made on the basis of your stated preferences and the needs of the departments, and it is not open to negotiation. [3] you have concerns about the arrangements, please raise them with your mentor in the first instance. You will be expected to [4] a short report on your experience at the end of the placement.

questions.explanation: 'So that you gain a broad understanding' gives the purpose of rotating departments; 'provided' needs 'that', 'in case' suggests a precaution, and 'lest' requires a negative idea.

choices: I recognize that every placement will coincide with the preference that you expressed in your application.
I recognize that not every placement will coincide with the preference that you expressed in your application.
I recognized that not every placement would coincide with the preference that you had expressed.
We recognize that not every candidate will coincide with the preference that the departments expressed.
questions.explanation: The next sentence explains how the allocation was made and that it is not negotiable, so the previous one should acknowledge that some placements may disappoint; only the first does. The others deny it, use past tenses, or confuse candidates and preferences.
'Should you have concerns' is an inverted conditional meaning 'if you have concerns'; the others cannot introduce it.
Participants must 'submit' a report; 'submerge' means put under water, 'subtract' means take away, and 'submit to' means yield.
